1	/**
2	 * Consumer views, version 1: the small shapes a patient-facing chart app reads.
3	 *
4	 * These are defined by the consumer, not by any source. A mapper turns one source's FOLIO record items
5	 * for one patient into these rows. The consumer merges rows from several sources itself, so a mapper
6	 * reports only what its own source says, and never invents, infers from other sources, or "corrects"
7	 * what the source records.
8	 *
9	 * Contract (see `Transform`): the mapper receives every item one source published for one patient,
10	 * in no particular order and including items that were later superseded or retracted, plus an
11	 * `asOf` date. It returns the rows that describe that source's record as it stood at the end of that
12	 * date.
13	 *
14	 * Conventions for every view:
15	 *
16	 * - **Scope in time.** An item is in scope when its envelope `recorded` time is on or before the end of
17	 *   the `asOf` day in America/Chicago. Ignore items recorded later. Apply the FOLIO correction rules to
18	 *   the items in scope: an item listed in another in-scope item's `supersedes` or `retracts` (same
19	 *   issuer) is not current; supersession is transitive. Use only current items, except where a view
20	 *   below says otherwise.
21	 * - **Time zone.** The consumer displays everything in America/Chicago. "Local date" and "local time"
22	 *   below mean wall-clock date/time in America/Chicago (UTC-6 standard, UTC-5 daylight time).
23	 * - **Partial dates.** `PartialDate` strings keep the precision the source actually knows: "2016"
24	 *   means some time in 2016, never 2016-01-01. Never pad a year-only or month-only date.
25	 * - **Only what the source records.** Rows come from structured payload entries. Narrative text may be
26	 *   used to understand an entry but must not be the only basis for a row.
27	 * - **Evidence.** Every row lists the items (and payload entry ids) it was built from, so the consumer
28	 *   can show the source text behind a fact.
29	 * - **Determinism.** Same input, same output: no clock, randomness, network or file access.
30	 */
31	
32	/** A FOLIO record item in its JSON form (see the FOLIO record-item spec). */
33	export interface FolioItem {
34	  folio: string;
35	  /** Item id (ULID), unique within the issuer. */
36	  id: string;
37	  /** did:web of the issuing organization. */
38	  issuer: string;
39	  /** Patient id at this issuer. */
40	  patient: string;
41	  /** When the clinical event happened: RFC 3339 date-time with offset, or a full or partial date. */
42	  effective: string;
43	  effective_end?: string;
44	  /** When the issuer committed this item: RFC 3339 date-time with offset. */
45	  recorded: string;
46	  author?: { id?: string; name?: string; role?: string };
47	  /** The payload's schema: `type` names the entry type in the source's .d.ts. */
48	  schema?: { url: string; type: string; sha256: string };
49	  /** Ids of earlier items from the same issuer that this item replaces entirely. */
50	  supersedes?: string[];
51	  /** Ids of earlier items from the same issuer that were entered in error, withdrawn without replacement. */
52	  retracts?: string[];
53	  /** Markdown narrative with `<ref id="…">…</ref>` spans; "" if none. */
54	  narrative: string;
55	  /** Entry id -> entry, each entry typed by the source's schema; {} if none. */
56	  payload: Record<string, any>;
57	}
58	
59	/** The mapper's entry point. `asOf` is a local date, `YYYY-MM-DD`. */
60	export type Transform = (items: FolioItem[], asOf: string) => ViewRows;
61	
62	/** Everything one mapper returns for one patient and one source. Empty arrays where the source has nothing. */
63	export interface ViewRows {
64	  medications: MedicationRow[];
65	  problems: ProblemRow[];
66	  allergies: AllergyIntoleranceRow[];
67	  labs: LabResultRow[];
68	  vitals: VitalRow[];
69	}
70	
71	/** `YYYY`, `YYYY-MM` or `YYYY-MM-DD`; the precision is the string's length. */
72	export type PartialDate = string;
73	
74	/** The items (and entries inside them) a row was built from. At least one. */
75	export type Evidence = { item_id: string; entry_id?: string }[];
76	
77	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
78	// Medications
79	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
80	
81	/**
82	 * One outpatient (home) medication as this source records it, with its status as of `asOf`.
83	 *
84	 * - One row per drug ingredient. If the source has several lines, orders or prescriptions for the
85	 *   same ingredient over time (stopped and restarted, re-entered), report the most recent one, i.e.
86	 *   the one whose own latest event is latest. A line or order that was entered in error, voided or
87	 *   retracted never existed: do not report it, and do not let it affect another line.
88	 * - Include medications that are stopped (status 'stopped') if the source still shows them, so the
89	 *   consumer can say what was stopped and why.
90	 * - Exclude hospital-only orders (infusions, IV fluids, inpatient-only drugs). They are not home
91	 *   medications.
92	 * - When the source publishes a medication list as repeated snapshots (each document or save restates
93	 *   the list), the latest in-scope snapshot is the source's list; a drug missing from the latest
94	 *   snapshot is not reported. When the source publishes events or status rows, the latest event or
95	 *   status row for a line determines its state, however old it is.
96	 */
97	export interface MedicationRow {
98	  /**
99	   * Generic ingredient name, lower case, without salt or form: "losartan" (not "losartan potassium"),
100	   * "metformin", "insulin glargine", "empagliflozin". Translate brand names the record uses
101	   * ("Jardiance" -> "empagliflozin"). Omit only when the record does not say which drug it is (e.g. the
102	   * patient wrote "water pill").
103	   */
104	  ingredient?: string;
105	  /** RxNorm ingredient CUI, only when the source states an ingredient-level RxNorm code. Never guessed or derived from a product code. */
106	  rxnorm_ingredient?: string;
107	  /** The drug as the source names it (display text), e.g. "losartan potassium 50 MG Oral Tablet" or "Jardiance". */
108	  drug_name: string;
109	  /**
110	   * Status as of `asOf`, by this source's account.
111	   * - 'active': the patient should be taking it (or, on a patient's own list, says they are).
112	   * - 'held': paused with intent (or at least possibility) of resuming; the patient should not be
113	   *   taking it now. Not the same as stopped.
114	   * - 'stopped': discontinued.
115	   * - 'unknown': the source lists the drug but records no decision about whether it is being taken
116	   *   (e.g. a hospital list marked as not reconciled).
117	   */
118	  status: 'active' | 'held' | 'stopped' | 'unknown';
119	  /**
120	   * Local date on which the current status began according to this source: for 'held' or 'stopped',
121	   * the date of the hold or stop; for 'active', the date the source's current line or order started
122	   * (or resumed). Keep the source's precision. Omit if the source does not say.
123	   */
124	  status_since?: PartialDate;
125	  /**
126	   * Amount per administration currently prescribed (for 'held' and 'stopped': the amount when it was
127	   * held or stopped). For a patient's own list: the amount the patient says they take, if they give
128	   * one. `unit` is one of the listed units; convert source spellings ("unit", "UNT", "[iU]" ->
129	   * "units"; "tab"/"tablets" -> "tablet"). Omit when the source gives no single amount.
130	   */
131	  dose?: { value: number; unit: 'mg' | 'mcg' | 'units' | 'mL' | 'tablet' };
132	  /**
133	   * How often, normalized: 'QD' once daily, 'BID' twice daily, 'TID' three times daily, 'QHS' once
134	   * daily at bedtime, 'QW' once weekly, 'PRN' as needed, 'other' anything else. Omit if unknown.
135	   */
136	  frequency?: 'QD' | 'BID' | 'TID' | 'QHS' | 'QW' | 'PRN' | 'other';
137	  /**
138	   * For 'stopped' rows, why, when the source records a coded or clearly stated reason:
139	   * - 'adverse_reaction': side effect or adverse reaction.
140	   * - 'ineffective': not working well enough.
141	   * - 'therapy_changed': replaced by another drug for the same purpose.
142	   * - 'course_complete': finite course finished.
143	   * - 'patient_choice': the patient declined or asked to stop.
144	   * - 'other': another reason (see `status_reason_text`).
145	   * Omit when the source gives no reason, and on rows that are not 'stopped'.
146	   */
147	  stop_reason?: 'adverse_reaction' | 'ineffective' | 'therapy_changed' | 'course_complete' | 'patient_choice' | 'other';
148	  /** Free-text reason for the current status (hold or stop) as the source wrote it, if any. */
149	  status_reason_text?: string;
150	  /** True when the row comes from the patient's own account (a self-reported list), not a clinician's record. */
151	  patient_reported: boolean;
152	  /** True when the source says the drug was bought without a prescription. Omit otherwise. */
153	  otc?: boolean;
154	  evidence: Evidence;
155	}
156	
157	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
158	// Problems
159	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
160	
161	/**
162	 * One condition on the source's problem list (or the source's equivalent: its diagnosis or history
163	 * lists), with status as of `asOf`.
164	 *
165	 * - One row per condition. Several entries for the same condition (re-listed in several documents,
166	 *   restaged, re-coded) are one row whose fields reflect the latest entry.
167	 * - Report only conditions the source asserts the patient has or had. Never report a condition that
168	 *   was ruled out, or one that was only suspected (working/provisional) and never confirmed.
169	 * - Billing codes attached to a visit or claim are not problem-list entries, unless the source says
170	 *   its problem list is built from them.
171	 * - An adverse effect of a drug (however the source records it, including as an ICD-10 T-code
172	 *   diagnosis) is an `AllergyIntoleranceRow` of type 'adverse_reaction', not a problem. The illness it
173	 *   caused (e.g. ketoacidosis) is still a problem.
174	 */
175	export interface ProblemRow {
176	  /** The condition as the source words it, e.g. "Chronic kidney disease stage 3a". */
177	  condition: string;
178	  /** ICD-10-CM code, with the dot, as the source gives it (latest). Omit if the source gives none. */
179	  icd10cm?: string;
180	  /** SNOMED CT concept id, if the source gives one. */
181	  snomed?: string;
182	  /**
183	   * - 'active': the patient has it.
184	   * - 'resolved': the patient had it and the source says it is resolved or historical.
185	   */
186	  status: 'active' | 'resolved';
187	  /** When the condition began, at the precision the source knows. Omit if the source does not say. */
188	  onset?: { value: PartialDate; precision: 'year' | 'month' | 'day' };
189	  /**
190	   * For chronic kidney disease only: the KDIGO GFR category the source most recently recorded for this
191	   * patient ('G3a' for "stage 3a", "N18.31" or a G3a category field). As recorded by a clinician; never
192	   * computed from lab values.
193	   */
194	  ckd_stage?: 'G1' | 'G2' | 'G3a' | 'G3b' | 'G4' | 'G5';
195	  /** For chronic kidney disease only: KDIGO albuminuria category as recorded ('A1', 'A2', 'A3'), if the source records one. */
196	  albuminuria?: 'A1' | 'A2' | 'A3';
197	  evidence: Evidence;
198	}
199	
200	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
201	// Allergies, intolerances, adverse reactions
202	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
203	
204	/**
205	 * One substance the patient should avoid or be careful with, as of `asOf`. Only current entries: an
206	 * entry the source marks inactive or invalid is not reported. "No known drug allergies" is not a row.
207	 */
208	export interface AllergyIntoleranceRow {
209	  /** Substance: generic ingredient name, lower case, for drugs ("lisinopril"); as written otherwise. */
210	  substance: string;
211	  /** RxNorm ingredient CUI, if the source gives one. */
212	  rxnorm_ingredient?: string;
213	  /**
214	   * What kind of reaction, by its nature (not by which list the source keeps it on):
215	   * - 'allergy': immune-mediated (hives, rash, angioedema, anaphylaxis, bronchospasm).
216	   * - 'intolerance': a non-immune, predictable side effect that made the drug unacceptable (e.g.
217	   *   ACE-inhibitor cough, GI upset).
218	   * - 'adverse_reaction': a serious harmful event attributed to the drug that is not an allergy (e.g.
219	   *   drug-associated ketoacidosis, lactic acidosis).
220	   * If the source keeps all three on one undifferentiated list, decide from the recorded reaction.
221	   */
222	  type: 'allergy' | 'intolerance' | 'adverse_reaction';
223	  /** Reaction(s) as the source words them, joined with "; ". Omit if not recorded. */
224	  reaction?: string;
225	  /**
226	   * Criticality: how dangerous re-exposure is judged to be.
227	   * - 'high': re-exposure could be serious or life-threatening.
228	   * - 'low': re-exposure unlikely to cause serious harm.
229	   * - 'unknown': not assessed or not derivable.
230	   * A source's "severity" scale is mapped by meaning: mild -> 'low'; severe or life-threatening -> 'high'.
231	   */
232	  criticality: 'low' | 'high' | 'unknown';
233	  /** When the reaction began, at the precision the source knows. */
234	  onset?: { value: PartialDate; precision: 'year' | 'month' | 'day' };
235	  evidence: Evidence;
236	}
237	
238	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
239	// Lab results
240	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
241	
242	/**
243	 * Analytes this consumer tracks, with the unit `LabResultRow.value` must be in. Results for other
244	 * tests are not reported.
245	 *
246	 * | analyte         | unit            | notes |
247	 * |-----------------|-----------------|-------|
248	 * | creatinine      | mg/dL           | serum |
249	 * | egfr            | mL/min/1.73m2   | see `egfr_equation` and the eGFR rule below |
250	 * | potassium       | mmol/L          | |
251	 * | sodium          | mmol/L          | |
252	 * | chloride        | mmol/L          | |
253	 * | bicarbonate     | mmol/L          | total CO2 |
254	 * | anion_gap       | mmol/L          | |
255	 * | bun             | mg/dL           | urea nitrogen |
256	 * | glucose         | mg/dL           | laboratory glucose (serum/plasma); home meter readings are vitals |
257	 * | a1c             | %               | NGSP |
258	 * | uacr            | mg/g            | urine albumin/creatinine ratio |
259	 * | platelets       | 10*3/uL         | thousands per microlitre: 212 000 cells/uL is 212 |
260	 * | wbc             | 10*3/uL         | thousands per microlitre |
261	 * | hemoglobin      | g/dL            | |
262	 * | bhb             | mmol/L          | beta-hydroxybutyrate |
263	 * | ph              | [pH]            | blood gas pH |
264	 * | pco2            | mmHg            | |
265	 * | lipase          | U/L             | |
266	 * | troponin        | ng/mL           | troponin I |
267	 * | cholesterol     | mg/dL           | total |
268	 * | triglycerides   | mg/dL           | |
269	 * | hdl             | mg/dL           | |
270	 * | ldl             | mg/dL           | measured or calculated |
271	 */
272	export type Analyte =
273	  | 'creatinine' | 'egfr' | 'potassium' | 'sodium' | 'chloride' | 'bicarbonate' | 'anion_gap' | 'bun'
274	  | 'glucose' | 'a1c' | 'uacr' | 'platelets' | 'wbc' | 'hemoglobin' | 'bhb' | 'ph' | 'pco2' | 'lipase'
275	  | 'troponin' | 'cholesterol' | 'triglycerides' | 'hdl' | 'ldl';
276	
277	/**
278	 * One valid laboratory result.
279	 *
280	 * - One row per result. A result the source shows several times (copies in several documents, a
281	 *   preliminary and a final copy) is one row, taken from the copy with the most advanced status.
282	 * - Report only values that stand: leave out results that were withdrawn, invalidated or "corrected
283	 *   away" by the lab, results of orders voided or entered in error, results not performed, and
284	 *   superseded copies. A confirmation repeat is a second valid result; keep both.
285	 * - **eGFR rule.** One eGFR row per eGFR calculation the source reports for a specimen. When the source
286	 *   reports race-specific variants of one calculation (a value with and one without a race
287	 *   coefficient), report only the variant without the race coefficient. Report the value as printed
288	 *   (do not recompute).
289	 */
290	export interface LabResultRow {
291	  analyte: Analyte;
292	  /** Numeric value in the analyte's unit (see `Analyte`). For a result printed with a comparator (">60", "<0.01"), the number part. */
293	  value: number;
294	  /** Set when the printed result has a comparator: ">60" -> value 60, comparator '>'. */
295	  comparator?: '<' | '>' | '<=' | '>=';
296	  /** The analyte's unit from the table in `Analyte`, exactly as written there. */
297	  unit: string;
298	  /** Specimen collection time, RFC 3339 with offset (any offset; it denotes an instant). */
299	  collected: string;
300	  /** 'final' (also for amended or corrected values that stand) or 'preliminary'. */
301	  status: 'final' | 'preliminary';
302	  /**
303	   * For analyte 'egfr' only: the equation the source says it used.
304	   * - 'ckd-epi-2021': CKD-EPI 2021 (race-free).
305	   * - 'ckd-epi-2009': CKD-EPI 2009.
306	   * - 'mdrd': MDRD.
307	   * - 'unknown': not stated.
308	   * When a code and a method note disagree, believe the method note.
309	   */
310	  egfr_equation?: 'ckd-epi-2021' | 'ckd-epi-2009' | 'mdrd' | 'unknown';
311	  /** LOINC code if the source gives one for this result. */
312	  loinc?: string;
313	  evidence: Evidence;
314	}
315	
316	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
317	// Vital signs and home readings
318	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
319	
320	/**
321	 * One set of vital signs taken together, or one home reading.
322	 *
323	 * - A clinic or hospital vital-sign set (BP, pulse, weight taken within a few minutes at one visit) is
324	 *   one row; `local_time` is the time of its first blood pressure (or of its first measurement if no
325	 *   BP). A repeat blood pressure taken later in the same visit goes in `repeat_*` on the same row.
326	 * - Each home BP reading and each home glucose reading is its own row.
327	 * - Each measurement is reported once: if a source shows the same measurement twice (a reading typed
328	 *   in by hand that duplicates one synced from the device a minute or two earlier with the same
329	 *   values), report it once, preferring the device copy.
330	 */
331	export interface VitalRow {
332	  /** 'clinic' (outpatient office), 'hospital' (ED or inpatient), or 'home' (patient's own devices). */
333	  setting: 'clinic' | 'hospital' | 'home';
334	  /** Local wall-clock time in America/Chicago, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM`. */
335	  local_time: string;
336	  systolic_mmhg?: number;
337	  diastolic_mmhg?: number;
338	  /** Repeat blood pressure at the same visit, if one was taken. */
339	  repeat_systolic_mmhg?: number;
340	  repeat_diastolic_mmhg?: number;
341	  pulse_bpm?: number;
342	  /** Body weight in kilograms (1 lb = 0.45359237 kg), one decimal place. */
343	  weight_kg?: number;
344	  /** Home glucose meter reading in mg/dL (1 mmol/L = 18.016 mg/dL), rounded to a whole number. */
345	  glucose_mg_dl?: number;
346	  /** Set when the meter showed HI or LO instead of a number; `glucose_mg_dl` is then the meter's limit in mg/dL. */
347	  glucose_out_of_range?: 'HI' | 'LO';
348	  evidence: Evidence;
349	}
